newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa sending aircraft to flooded Mozambique.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa sending aircraft to flooded Mozambique.

text.p: South Africa said on Friday it would send aircraft to remove people threatened by rising flood waters in neighbouring Mozambique.

South Africa's Department of Foreign Affairs said in a statement Mozambique's second largest city Beira had been cut off and thousands of people were forced to flee their homes after heavy flooding in Manhica and Sofala provinces.

A South Africa Air Force Caravan aircraft was deployed on Friday to make a survey of the flooded areas. Two helicopters would be deployed later and a C130 aircraft was on standby to transport ground crew if necessary, air force spokeswoman Laverne Machine told Reuters.
The statement said Mozambique's Foreign Minister Leonardo Simao had told his South African counterpart that local authorities could not cope with the flood damage.
"In collaboration with the South African National Defence Force...emergency aircraft and helicopters will be sent to the area," the statement said.
"Minister Simao emphasised that the immediate concern of the Mozambican government was to airlift people from areas along the Punge river," the statement said.
It said thousands of heactares (acres) of crops had been submerged by waters from the Pungue, Buzi and Save rivers in Sofala province. Road and rail transport had also been affected.
"The Pungue valley has been turned into an enormous lake with only the tops of ruined huts visible above the flood water level," it said.
